items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: He used to call me Big Jim. Why, I don't know, but that's what he, Monarchy, laid on me.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. I see. So some of the guys would be faking, but the others would read their parts. That's right. And not, you didn't try to make it anything special, just like it was written. I see. What happened to Charlie Dixon?

Charlie Dixon passed about three or five years ago. He died in San Antonio, Texas. He was a wonderful musician and a great fellow. In fact, Charlie Dixon was more of a father to the band. Everybody looked up at Charlie Dixon as an advisor. And he was exceptionally crazy about me. He used to call me Big Jim. Why, I don't know, but that's what he, Monarchy, laid on me.
I wondered about that band. A whole lot of things, you know. He seemed to have a quite unusual style. I never heard anybody else play trombone quite like Charlie Dixon.
